title: Frankly Speaking: The Company Election Integrity Keeps in Congressional Communication
abstract: arXiv:2610.36187v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Election integrity is a shared commitment in American politics, but Democrats and Republicans in Congress increasingly mean different things by it. Analyzing 10,420 congressional e-newsletters sent from 2010 to 2025, we examine how the two parties invoke election terms such as ``integrity,'' ``security,'' and ``fraud.'' Using diachronic word embeddings, which track semantic change through how words are used in context, we measure how differently each party uses each term, how much each party shifts, and whether they share nearest semantic neighbors. We show that members of Congress do not need different words to tell different stories about elections. They need only place those same words in different company. Across nearly every term and year, the two parties surround election-integrity vocabulary with entirely different words. translated_title: 直言不讳：国会传播中“选举诚信”一词的语境伙伴
translated_abstract: 选举诚信是美国政治中各方共同承诺的价值，但国会中的民主党人和共和党人对它的理解却日益分化。我们分析了2010年至2025年间发送的10,420份国会电子简报，考察两党如何使用“诚信”、“安全”、“舞弊”等选举词汇。借助历时词嵌入方法——通过词语在上下文中的使用来追踪语义变化——我们测量了两党对每个词汇的使用差异程度、各自的变化幅度，以及双方是否共享最邻近的语义邻居。研究显示，国会议员无需使用不同的词汇就能讲述关于选举的不同故事，他们只需将相同的词汇置于不同的“伙伴”（上下文）之中。在几乎每一个任期和每一年，两党都会用完全不同的词汇来围绕选举诚信词汇展开论述。这种分歧很容易被忽视，因为大多数选举词汇的分化程度并不比同时期使用的其他词汇更高。
tldr: 本研究利用历时词嵌入方法分析2010至2025年间的10,420份国会电子简报，发现民主党和共和党虽然使用相同的“选举诚信”词汇，却将其置于截然不同的语义语境中，从而用同样的词讲述不同的政治故事。
en_tdlr: Using diachronic word embeddings on 10,420 congressional e-newsletters (2010–2025), this study shows that Democrats and Republicans convey divergent election narratives not through different words, but by embedding the same election-integrity vocabulary in entirely different semantic contexts.
